recognize_zh: Romanowsky 染色下漿細胞質內充滿大小不一的淡藍色圓形包涵體（Russell 小體，Mott 細胞）；同一類細胞在 Papanicolaou 染色則呈現鮮明的橘色圓球，是 Russell 小體在巴氏染色的特徵顏色。
features: Panel A: plasma cells with eccentric, sometimes binucleated nuclei and deeply basophilic cytoplasm
Panel A: numerous small round pale-blue to clear globular inclusions distending the cytoplasm and cytoplasmic blebs (Russell bodies, Mott cell pattern)
Panels Bi and Bii (Papanicolaou): cells containing multiple round, refractile, orange-colored globules of varying size packing the cytoplasm
Inclusions are homogeneous and sharply demarcated, consistent with condensed immunoglobulin
Adjacent cells in Bii without inclusions for comparison
describe_en: The Romanowsky-stained preparation shows plasma cells, including a binucleated form, with deeply basophilic cytoplasm filled with multiple round pale globular inclusions, consistent with Mott cells containing Russell bodies. On Papanicolaou staining, similar cells contain numerous sharply circumscribed, homogeneous orange globules. Recognizing the orange color of Russell bodies on Pap stain prevents misinterpretation as pigment, mucin or microorganisms. Findings are consistent with plasma cells containing Russell bodies (Mott cells), which can occur in reactive plasmacytosis or plasma cell neoplasms.

ddx.vs: Hemosiderin is coarse golden-brown and irregular in macrophages with Prussian blue positivity, rather than uniform round orange globules in plasma cells.
Signet-ring cells have a single large mucin vacuole displacing the nucleus and are cytokeratin positive, not multiple small immunoglobulin globules.
Dutcher bodies are single intranuclear pseudoinclusions overlying the nucleus rather than multiple cytoplasmic globules.
Yeasts have a cell wall, budding and variable staining, and are often extracellular, unlike homogeneous intracytoplasmic globules.
